solution_full: The bracket is a geometric progression with ratio $2$: $1+2+\cdots+2^{n-1}=2^n-1$.
So the $n$-th term is $\dfrac{n(2^n-1)}{6^n}=n\left(\dfrac13\right)^n-n\left(\dfrac16\right)^n$: the sequence of terms is converted into the difference of two arithmetico-geometric sequences.

For $|x|<1$ let $S(x)=\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}nx^n$. Then $S-xS=\displaystyle\sum_{n\ge1}x^n=\frac{x}{1-x}$, so $S(x)=\dfrac{x}{(1-x)^2}$; both series converge, so they may be subtracted term by term.
originality_note: New: the coefficient of each term is itself a GP partial sum, so the series is converted into a difference of two AGPs whose ratios 1/3 and 1/6 give exact two-decimal values (way 5: GP partial sums linked with AGP sums). Closest known: 'sum n/3^n' and 'sum (2^n - 1)/3^n' exercises. Different because: the n-weight and the GP partial sum appear together, so both conversions are needed.
blueprint_concepts: Sum of an Arithmetico Geometric Progression

concept_use.Sequences convertible to GP: The term n(2^n - 1)/6^n is converted into n(1/3)^n - n(1/6)^n, a difference of two GP-type sequences.
concept_use.Sum of an Arithmetico Geometric Progress: Each part is an AGP summed by S - xS, giving 3/4 and 6/25.
